howItWorks.title: How InvestFund works
howItWorks.intro: A clear path from discovery to a recorded funding outcome, with both sides in control.

s1.title: 1. Founders publish
s1.body: Founders sign in with Google, create a startup profile and add funding milestones. A startup can only be published once the required details are complete: what it does, its sector, stage and location, how much it needs (a target inside an acceptable range) and at least one milestone.

s2.title: 2. Supporters discover
s2.body: Supporters set their preferences: sectors, stages, purposes, places and a typical amount. Recommendations are ranked with a transparent, weighted score and explained in plain language. Anyone can search and filter published startups.

s3.title: 3. Connect and talk
s3.body: A supporter asks to connect. The founder accepts or declines. Only after acceptance does a private, real-time conversation open, and founders can share confidential documents with the people they choose.

s4.title: 4. Agree terms
s4.body: Either side proposes a grant or donation: amount, currency, purpose, conditions and milestones. The other side can accept, decline or counter. Every revision is kept, so both of you always see the full history.

s5.title: 5. Record the outcome
s5.body: Money moves directly between you, outside InvestFund. The supporter reports sending it and the founder confirms receipt; disagreements and cancellations are recorded rather than overwritten. InvestFund never processes payments and does not verify transfers.

privacy.notice: Placeholder text for development. This notice has not been reviewed by a qualified legal adviser and must be replaced before launch.

s1.title: What we collect
s1.body: From Google sign-in: your name, email address, profile picture and a Google account identifier. From you: profile details, preferences, startup listings, messages, proposals, documents and reports.

s2.title: How it is used
s2.body: To run the marketplace: showing published startups, recommending matches from your stated preferences, delivering messages and notifications, and keeping a record of negotiations and outcomes. Your email address is not shown to other users.

s3.title: Who can see what
s3.body: Published startup profiles are public. Messages, proposals and outcomes are visible only to the two parties. Confidential documents are visible only to the founder and connections they allow. Administrators can see reports and the records needed to review them.

s4.title: Retention and your rights
s4.body: Retention periods, lawful bases, data subject rights handling and international transfers are open questions for legal review. Until self-service tools exist, contact the team to request access to or deletion of your data.

s5.title: Contact
s5.body: Contact details will be added before launch.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.notice: Placeholder text for development. These terms have not been reviewed by a qualified legal adviser and must be replaced before launch.

s1.title: What InvestFund is
s1.body: InvestFund helps founders and supporters find each other, talk and record agreed grants or donations. It is not a payment service, crowdfunding platform, investment platform, regulated financial service or contract signer.

s2.title: No payments, no verification
s2.body: All money moves directly between users, outside the platform. Accepted proposals and reported outcomes are statements by users. InvestFund does not verify identities, businesses or transfers.

s3.title: Not a legal agreement
s3.body: Accepting a proposal records agreement on InvestFund only. If you need a binding agreement, arrange one separately with appropriate advice.

s4.title: Acceptable use
s4.body: Do not post misleading information, impersonate others, harass users or request sensitive financial credentials. You can block users and report profiles or listings; administrators may archive listings or suspend accounts.

s5.title: Questions for legal review
s5.body: Fundraising and charitable-donation rules, consumer protection, liability, tax receipts and jurisdiction must be reviewed before launch.
